title: The fuzzy operators ~= and ~* never lex, so a fuzzy query silently degrades to a label-existence or match-everything query
statement: The manual documents #title ~= trilim and #content ~* progra as fuzzy operators with a minimum term length and a maximum edit distance. In the lexer a bare '~' unconditionally starts a new attribute token, so it can never become the first character of a two-character operator, parseLabel never sees ~= or ~*, and the query falls through to label existence. The comparators for both operators exist and are correct but are unreachable from the query language. The operand is not merely mis-ranked, it is not consulted at all: #tcfuzzy ~= qqqqqqq, which shares no character with either stored value, still returns both labelled notes, and note.content ~* zzzzznotpresent returns the whole tree.

handVerified.note: Report section 1. Controls show the label, the values and the comparator machinery are all sound: '=' splits the two notes correctly and bare label existence returns both, so only '~' fails. One divergence recorded: #9426 reports 'Unrecognized expression books' for note.title ~= Books, but on this build the property-path forms answer 200 [] silently and note.content ~* answers 200 with the whole tree, so the visible-error half of the original finding does not reproduce here.

source.howDecided: No commit touches lex.ts between the tested commit and head; the blob is identical at tested, head and v0.105.0. Re-read at head: :96-105 still contains the unconditional `if (chr === "#" || chr === "~") { ... currentWord = chr; continue; }`. Not fixed on main. Open PR #10633 contains the exact fix as a single 12-line hunk inserted at :93-105, adding `if (chr === "~" && fulltextEnded && (str[i+1] === "=" || str[i+1] === "*"))` to emit the two-character operator; PR #9508 is a standalone fix for the same thing but is unmerged with mergeable_state 'dirty' and untouched since 2026-07-13.

citedItems.note: Still open, labels State: Triage / awaiting feedback / search, last updated 2026-05-02, 3 comments. Reported against 0.102.2 and its entire body is three quoted ERROR messages (Unrecognized expression, Misplaced or incomplete expression). On 0.105.0 none of those errors appear; the same queries answer 200 with [] or with the whole tree. So the issue covers the defect but its stated symptom is stale, and a maintainer checking it today could wrongly conclude it was fixed.
Titled 'fix(search): tokenize ~= and ~* as single fuzzy-match operators', says Fixes #9426. Not updated since 2026-07-13 and now conflicting with main; effectively superseded by #10633.
Verified this pass at the file level: its lex.ts hunk is exactly the fix for this finding. It is the live thread (updated the day before the current release) and the only one that is mergeable.

newItems.title: Search Issues
newItems.note: The umbrella search-quality issue that PR #10633 answers. It reports fuzzy inconsistency by example (sync finds Send, but combinef does not find combined) plus ranking, highlighting and navigation complaints. It does not name the ~= / ~* operators or the lexer, so it is adjacent rather than a duplicate.

reevaluation: The finding still reproduces on main and in release v0.105.0, but it is reported and a mergeable fix is in flight, so a new issue would be a duplicate. Nothing moved since the report: #9426 open and untouched since May, #9508 open and now conflicting, #10633 open, clean and freshly updated. Two things are worth contributing rather than filing. First, #9426's symptom is stale: it quotes error messages that 0.105.0 no longer produces, and the current behaviour is silent (200 [] for the property-path form, the whole tree for note.content ~*), which is both harder to notice and easy to mistake for a fix. Second, the report's decisive probe is stronger than anything on the thread: ~= with an operand sharing no character with either stored value still returns both notes, which shows the operand is never consulted, not merely mis-scored. Both belong on the live PR thread, which FILING-GUIDE treats as cheap and welcome.
notes: Do not open a new issue. The comment should confirm the defect is live in v0.105.0, quote the ~= qqqqqqq probe and the note.content ~* whole-tree answer, and state that the PR's lex.ts hunk is the fix. If a second action is wanted, add the same correction to #9426 so its stale error-message symptom does not get it closed as fixed. Note that #10633 does NOT fix F6, F8, F9 or F13 even though it edits three of the same files; check the per-file analysis in those JSONs before claiming otherwise on the thread.
